summary: The Yuma County Library District serves Yuma County, Arizona, and currently includes a nearly 80,000 square foot Main Library in Yuma plus several branches across the county. The note traces its origin to the first Yuma Library, a Carnegie library that opened in 1921 in Sunset Park. That building was expanded and renovated over the years, including a $4.2 million renovation completed in 2009, and it still operates today as the Heritage Branch Library.
one_line: Overview of the Yuma County Library District in Arizona, its branches, and the history of its Carnegie library building.
key_facts: The Yuma County Library District serves the population of Yuma County, Arizona.
The Main Library of the Yuma County Library District is nearly 80,000 square feet and is located in Yuma.
The library district includes branches in downtown Yuma, the Foothills, Somerton, San Luis, Wellton, Dateland, and Roll.
The first Yuma Library was a Carnegie library.
The first Yuma Library opened February 24, 1921.
The first Yuma Library opened with 1,053 volumes.
The first Yuma Library had seating for 20 persons.
The Yuma Carnegie Library is located in Sunset Park.
The Yuma Carnegie Library underwent several expansions and renovations over the years.
A $4.2 million renovation of the Yuma Carnegie Library was completed in 2009.
The Yuma Carnegie Library still operates today as the Heritage Branch Library in downtown Yuma.
